extraction.name: FLEURS
extraction.description: An n-way parallel speech dataset in 102 languages built on top of the FLoRes-101 benchmark, with approximately 12 hours of speech supervision per language. It is designed for tasks including ASR, Speech LangID, translation, and retrieval.
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Min Ma, Simran Khanuja, Yu Zhang, Vera Axelrod, Siddharth Dalmia, Jason Riesa, Clara Rivera, Ankur Bapna
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was built on top of FLoRes-101. The authors split the dev and devtest sentences into new train/dev/test splits, then collected three speech recordings per sentence from three different native speakers, with additional workers validating whether each recording matched the input sentence. Invalid recordings were discarded. Source transcripts were reused from human translators, and the English translated transcripts were maintained.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: About 21.5% of the sentences were missing in the first version because none of the three recordings were validated; the authors state they plan to fill these gaps in future versions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Speech recordings in 102 languages, with three recordings per sentence from native speakers; source text sentences came from FLoRes-101, which contains 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and translated into 101 languages by human translators.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For each sentence in the 102 languages, three recordings were collected by three different native speakers; each recording was then evaluated by additional workers to assess whether it corresponded to the input sentence, and invalid recordings were discarded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality control was performed by additional workers validating whether recordings matched the input sentence; invalid recordings were discarded. The paper also states that the dataset has strong quality control.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Three recordings per sentence were collected, by three different native speakers.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Native speakers; sex ratio was balanced to at least 30/70% when possible.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset spans 102 languages and is intended to support diverse multilingual research, but the paper does not explicitly discuss specific demographic or sampling biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is positioned for evaluation of few-shot multilingual speech representations and downstream tasks such as ASR, translation, classification, and retrieval; the paper does not state explicit limitations or non-recommended uses in the provided section.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to catalyze research toward multilingual speech technologies and progress toward speech technologies for everyone.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Suitable for ASR, Speech-to-Text and Speech-to-Speech Translation, Speech LangID, and Multilingual Speech-to-Speech and Speech-to-Text Retrieval; also used for evaluation and baseline fine-tuning of multilingual pretrained models.

name.evidence: We introduce FLEURS, the Few-shot Learning Evaluation of Universal Representations of Speech benchmark.

description.evidence: FLEURS is an n-way parallel speech dataset in 102 languages built on top of the machine translation FLoRes-101 benchmark, with approximately 12 hours of speech supervision per language. FLEURS can be used for a variety of speech tasks, including Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Speech Language Identification (Speech LangID), Translation and Retrieval.

url.evidence: The dataset is publicly available via TFDS at https://tensorflow.org/datasets/catalog/xtreme_s and Huggingface at https://hf.co/datasets/google/xtreme_s.
